DOCUMENT:
Vendor Comparison: Standard Parcel Delivery Contract
Larkspur Home, Operations, June 2026

1. Purpose
Our contract with our current standard-delivery carrier ends on 30 September 2026. This paper compares three shortlisted carriers and recommends which should carry our standard (two-to-four-day) parcels from October.

2. Volumes and requirements
We dispatch an average of 42,000 standard parcels a month: about 70% weigh under 2 kg (cushions, textiles, small homeware) and 30% weigh 2 to 10 kg (lamps, mirrors, small furniture). Our requirements are on-time delivery of at least 95%, a damage rate below 0.5%, full tracking, and a returns service.

Damage and loss matter to us commercially. Each damaged or lost parcel costs us on average £48 in replacement stock, return shipping and customer service time, and damaged items are the most common cause of one-star reviews.

3. Trial
Between 1 April and 31 May 2026, each shortlisted carrier delivered a share of our orders, allocated at random by the warehouse management system, about 5,000 parcels per carrier. We measured on-time delivery against the promised date, damage reported by customers within 14 days, and lost parcels.

Table 1. Prices and trial performance
Carrier | Price, under 2 kg | Price, 2-10 kg | On-time delivery | Damage rate | Lost per 10,000 parcels
SwiftDrop | £3.10 | £4.60 | 96.2% | 0.4% | 3
ParcelLine | £2.85 | £4.95 | 93.1% | 0.9% | 8
Meridian | £3.30 | £4.40 | 97.5% | 0.3% | 2

On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial, and all three offer full tracking and a returns service.

4. Cost comparison
Applying our 70/30 weight mix, the average cost per parcel is £3.55 for SwiftDrop, £3.48 for ParcelLine and £3.63 for Meridian. On 42,000 parcels a month, the monthly cost would be £149,100 for SwiftDrop, £146,160 for ParcelLine and £152,460 for Meridian. ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop and £6,300 a month against Meridian, or between about £35,000 and £76,000 a year.

5. Customer contact
"Where is my order?" contacts are our largest single category of customer service enquiry. During the trial, ParcelLine deliveries generated 6 such contacts per 1,000 parcels, compared with 11 for SwiftDrop and 10 for Meridian. ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts, and at an average handling cost of £3.20 per contact this would save about £670 a month at our volumes. From 1 May, ParcelLine parcels also carried our new proactive delivery-day text message, which we were testing on one carrier before rolling it out.

6. Other considerations
All three carriers can collect from our warehouse daily at 6 pm. ParcelLine and SwiftDrop offer a 12-month contract; Meridian requires 24 months. SwiftDrop and Meridian have both handled our peak-season volumes for other retailers of similar size, while ParcelLine's references were mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels.

All three carriers integrate with our warehouse management system through standard interfaces, and none would require changes to our packing process or labelling. Each offers recipients a delivery-preference service to nominate a safe place or a neighbour, and each provides proof-of-delivery photographs, which our customer service team has found useful in resolving disputes.

7. Recommendation
ParcelLine offers the lowest delivery cost, met our service requirements in the trial and reduces customer contacts through its tracking app. We recommend awarding the standard parcel contract to ParcelLine for 12 months from 1 October 2026, saving up to £76,000 a year against the alternatives.

KEY (three known flaws):
1. [misread_evidence] at: "On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial" -- Table 1 shows ParcelLine's on-time delivery was 93.1%, below the 95% requirement. The claim (and the recommendation that ParcelLine 'met our service requirements') misreads the table; ParcelLine's 0.9% damage rate also fails the stated 0.5% requirement.
2. [unsupported_causal] at: "ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts" -- The document states that from 1 May ParcelLine parcels alone also carried the new proactive delivery-day text message. That concurrent intervention confounds the comparison, so the lower contact rate cannot be attributed to ParcelLine's tracking app.
3. [missing_consideration] at: "ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop" -- The cost comparison ignores the stated £48 cost of each damaged or lost parcel. ParcelLine's damage and loss rates (0.9% and 8 per 10,000) versus SwiftDrop's (0.4% and 3 per 10,000) imply about 231 extra problem parcels a month (about £11,100), far exceeding the £2,940 price saving; ParcelLine is likely the most expensive option overall.

REVIEW:
# Review: Vendor Comparison, Standard Parcel Delivery Contract

The pricing arithmetic is correct, but the recommendation doesn't follow from the evidence. **ParcelLine fails two of the four stated requirements in the trial, and once damage and loss are costed, it is the most expensive option.** The paper needs to be reworked before it goes forward.

## Critical issues

### 1. The service claim contradicts Table 1
Section 3 says "On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers," and the recommendation says ParcelLine "met our service requirements." The table shows otherwise:

| Requirement | Threshold | SwiftDrop | ParcelLine | Meridian |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| On-time | ≥ 95% | 96.2% ✅ | **93.1% ❌** | 97.5% ✅ |
| Damage | < 0.5% | 0.4% ✅ | **0.9% ❌** | 0.3% ✅ |

ParcelLine is the only carrier that fails, and it fails twice. With about 5,000 parcels each, these gaps are large enough that they're unlikely to be noise (e.g. roughly 45 damaged parcels for ParcelLine against 20 for SwiftDrop). The claim that "we are not trading reliability for price" is not supported.

### 2. The cost comparison leaves out damage and loss, which reverses the result
Section 2 says each damaged or lost parcel costs £48, but Section 4 ignores this. Including it at 42,000 parcels a month:

| | Delivery cost | Damage + loss rate | Incidents/month | Incident cost/month | **Total/month** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SwiftDrop | £149,100 | 0.43% | ~181 | ~£8,670 | **~£157,770** |
| ParcelLine | £146,160 | 0.98% | ~412 | ~£19,760 | **~£165,920** |
| Meridian | £152,460 | 0.32% | ~134 | ~£6,450 | **~£158,910** |

On a total-cost basis, ParcelLine costs about **£8,150 a month (~£98,000 a year) more than SwiftDrop**, not £35,000–£76,000 less. Late deliveries add further cost (more contacts and reviews) that isn't counted here, which would widen the gap. ParcelLine also has a reputational cost, since Section 2 names damage as the main cause of one-star reviews.

### 3. The customer-contact finding is confounded
Section 5 credits ParcelLine's lower "where is my order?" rate to its tracking app. But the same section says ParcelLine parcels alone carried the new proactive delivery-day text from 1 May, which is half the trial. The trial can't separate the two effects, and the text is the more plausible cause. Since the text is due to roll out on every carrier, any benefit it brings isn't specific to ParcelLine.

Even if the whole effect were real, the figure is small:
- The ~£670/month saving is measured against SwiftDrop only. Against Meridian it is ~£540.
- Either figure is far outweighed by ParcelLine's extra ~£11,000/month in damage and loss costs.

As a smaller point, the author's note says "barely half." The actual ratios are 55% and 60%.

## Other issues

- **"Up to £76,000 a year" overstates the saving.** The relevant comparison is with the next-cheapest option (SwiftDrop), which gives ~£35,000 on delivery price alone, and that disappears once issue 2 is counted.
- **Peak-season risk is understated.** The contract starts on 1 October, heading into the busiest quarter, but the trial ran in April–May. ParcelLine's references are mainly lighter-parcel fashion retailers, while SwiftDrop and Meridian have handled peak for similar retailers. ParcelLine is also the most expensive carrier for our 2–10 kg items (lamps, mirrors, furniture), which are also the items most likely to break.
- **ParcelLine's price advantage depends on the weight mix.** Against SwiftDrop, it disappears if items under 2 kg fall below about 58% of volume. A sensitivity line would help.
- **The loss figures rest on very small counts.** At ~5,000 parcels, 3 per 10,000 is about 1–2 parcels. Report the raw counts, and treat loss as indicative rather than conclusive. Damage and on-time are the stronger signals.
- **The trial didn't directly measure returns or tracking quality.** It's fine that the paper says all three offer them, but it should note this was confirmed by specification, not by the trial.

## What holds up
- The weighted per-parcel costs (£3.55 / £3.48 / £3.63), monthly totals and differences are all correct.
- Randomised allocation through the warehouse system is a good trial design and makes the head-to-head figures credible.
- Section 6's integration and operational points are useful and appear even-handed.

## Suggested direction
On the evidence presented, **SwiftDrop** looks like the strongest choice. It meets all requirements, has the lowest total cost, and offers the 12-month term the author values. **Meridian** has the best service and costs only ~£1,100/month more in total, but requires a 24-month commitment. That trade-off is worth setting out explicitly.

To revise the paper:
1. Correct the on-time and damage statements to match Table 1.
2. Add a total-cost table that includes damage and loss at £48.
3. Re-state the contact finding with the text-message confound, or remove it.
4. Address peak-season readiness given the October start.
5. Re-base the recommendation on total cost and requirement compliance.
